chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, raising it to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) that he used to say:

O Allah, I and this day are two creations from Your creations. O Allah, do not test me with it, nor test it with me. O Allah, do not let me be seen as audacious in disobeying You, nor as indulging in Your prohibitions. O Allah, turn away from me the doom, the adversities, the afflictions, the evil decrees, the gloating of the enemies, and the evil sight in myself and my wealth.

He said: And there is no servant who says when evening comes and when morning comes, 'I am pleased with Allah as Lord, and with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as Prophet, and with the Quran as the announcer, and with Ali as Imam' three times, except that it becomes a right upon Allah, the Mighty, the Compeller, to please him on the Day of Judgment.

He said: And he used to say (peace be upon him) when evening comes: 'In the morning we are grateful to Allah, and in the evening we are praising Allah. So for You is the praise just as we came to You in the evening as submitters, safe.'

He said: And when morning comes, he said: 'We have come to the evening as grateful to Allah, and we have come to the morning as praising Allah. And the praise is to Allah just as we came to You in the morning as submitters, safe.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.بِالْقُرْآنِ بَلَاغاً: With the Quran as the announcer/messenger
key_terms.رَضِيتُ بِاللَّهِ رَبّاً: I am pleased with Allah as Lord

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended morning and evening supplications in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi highlights the Shia tradition of *Adhkar al-Sha' wa al-Masa'* (morning and evening remembrances), linking daily spiritual discipline to divine protection from *Azl* (calamity) and *Shamatat al-A'da'* (gloating of enemies). The emphasis on reciting satisfaction with the Five Essentials (Allah, Islam, Muhammad, Quran, and Ali) three times reflects the theological centrality of *Imamah* in securing Allah's pleasure, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegesis of the Verse of Purification and the Verse of Mubahala.

en.hubeali: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, (It has been narrated) raising it to Amir Al-Momineenasws that heasws was saying: ‘(You should be saying), ‘O Allahazwj!

I<sup>asws</sup> and this day are two creations from Your<sup>azwj</sup> creations. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Neither Involve me with it nor involve it with me, and let not me be seen as audacious upon disobeying You<sup>azwj</sup>, nor as indulging in Your<sup>azwj</sup> Prohibitions. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Exchange from me the doom, and the adversities, and the afflictions, and the evil decisions, and the gloating of the enemies, and the evil scenes within myself and my wealth’.

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘And there is none from a servant saying when it is evening and morning, ‘I am pleased with Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> as Lord<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, and with Al-Islam as Religion, and with Muhammad<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> as a Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, and with the Quran as notification, and with Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> as an Imam<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>’, three times, except that he would have a right upon Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, the Mighty, the Compeller that He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Pleases him on the Day of Judgment’.

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘And he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> was saying when it was evening, ‘In the morning we are grateful to Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, and in the evening we are praising ones. So for You<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is the Praise just as we have come to You<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> in the evening as subbmitters, safe’’.  
He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘And when it was evening, he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘We have come to the evening as ones grateful to Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, and we have come to the morning has ones praising to Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, just as we had come to You<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> as submitters, safe’’.
en.sarwar: 12. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Muhammad ibn Ali in a marfu’ manner from Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) who has said the following: “

O Lord, I and this day are two creatures of Your creatures. O Lord, do not make me suffer from it and do not make it suffer from me. O Lord, do not allow it see me bold in disobeying You or committing unlawful things. O Lord, remove from me constraint and poverty, affliction and evil determination, and expression of joy from the enemy for bad things in me, and from being placed on an evil position, my property or myself. “

The Imam has said, ‘Any servant (of Allah) who says in the morning or evening three times, “I accept that Allah is my Lord, Islam is my religion, Muhammad (a.s.) is the Prophet, the Holy Quran is the text of Divine message and Ali (a.s.) is my Imam,” three times, it will be a right upon Allah, the Majestic, the Compeller to make him happy on the Day of Judgment. ’ “

The Imam has said that he (Ali, recipient of divine supreme covenant) would say in the evening, ‘We live in the morning thankful to Allah and we live in the evening praising Allah. All praise belongs to You as we live in the evening submitted to Y our will and in peace. ‘

‘The Imam said, ‘He (Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib, recipient of divine supreme covenant) in the morning would say, “We live in the evening thankful to Allah and we live in the morning praising Allah, all praise belongs to Allah. We live in the morning submitted to Your will and in peace.’”
